correctness.rationale: For p>=5 the published Theorem 1.3 gives the precise normalized extension bound and proves any nonzero maximizer has constant modulus. With f=c z, |z|=1, character orthogonality yields the exact p^-4 sum of squared ordered triple-fiber sums. Since the constant phase saturates the global sharp value and each fiber obeys |C_{s,r}|<=c^3 R_{s,r}, any maximizer must have all triple products z_u z_v z_w equal on each fiber. The translated triples (t,t+3,t+3) and (t+1,t+1,t+4) have the same sum and square-sum and give z_t z_{t+3}^2=z_{t+1}^2 z_{t+4}. Defining successive multiplicative differences, the third difference w obeys w_t w_{t+1}=1, hence w_{t+2}=w_t. Since p is odd, w_t is a constant sign, and telescoping product_t w_t=1 excludes -1. Therefore the second difference beta is constant, beta^p=1, and the first difference alpha obeys alpha^p=1; this gives exactly z_t=z_0 alpha^t beta^{t(t-1)/2}, the p-th root quadratic chirps. Modulation translates target frequencies and proves sufficiency, and a degree<=2 nonzero polynomial has fewer than p roots, yielding exactly p^2 distinct projective orbits. Independently reconstructed the exact pinned seven-blob Git tree and checked the full ordered triple-fiber multiplicity formula, energy, translated relations, and candidate phase exponents for p=5,7,11,13,17. The finite checks are only supporting examples; the proof works uniformly for all stated primes. The claim excludes p=2,3, prime-power extensions and zero function projective counting.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge new equality-set characterization for the sharp one-dimensional prime-field parabola L2-to-L6 inequality. The exact antecedent proves the sharp constant and constant modulus, but does not classify which unimodular phases attain equality. The new translated triple collision supplies the missing rigidity. The apparently stronger 2025/2026 moment-curve theorems concern the L2-to-L^{2d} endpoint; d=2 is L4 on (t,t^2), while d=3 is L6 on (t,t^2,t^3), so these do not imply the L6 planar-parabola phase classification. No independent earlier exact orbit listing was found; all searches are non-exhaustive.

value.rationale: A canonical sharp Fourier-extension inequality already had a proved best constant and necessary modulus, but not an exact phase equality set. The theorem settles this natural optimizer-classification gap for all primes >=5, identifies every possible complex extremizer as one of exactly p² projective quadratic-character classes, and explains why the relevant balanced three-term moment equations induce finite-difference rigidity. It is not an arbitrary small sample, recomputation of the sharp constant, or an unmotivated invariant; full equality characterization of a sharp natural inequality is independently useful. A general theory for prime powers or quantitative stability is not required for this result to have value.
residual_risks: Proof of the sharp constant and constant-modulus necessity is imported published mathematics, not a new contribution.
The classification is only for prime fields p>=5; no extension-field or stability claim is established.

limitations: The general sharp L2-to-L6 inequality and necessity of constant modulus are published Theorem 1.3 of arXiv:2405.16647, not new here.
Complete equality classification is only for prime fields p>=5 and nonzero functions modulo scalar; p=2,3, extensions and quantitative stability are not established.
Best-of-knowledge originality remains subject to older unindexed Freiman/finite-field Strichartz literature.
